parsed.explanation: The quote is §3's exhaustive dichotomy, and the objection reads it correctly. The preceding result only rules out two distinct POSITIVE values; nothing in the text excludes negative values of g. §1 gives only g(x)>−x; the identities (5)–(8) don't help; §4–§7 all presuppose V⊆{0,c} (Lemma 1 explicitly says 'b=g(z) belongs to {0,c}'), and §7's conclusion relies on the dichotomy. The objector's repair is mathematically valid: if g(x)=a<0, then (4) inductively yields g(x+na)=a with x+na=f(x+(n−1)a)>0 for all n, while x+na→−∞, contradicting f:>0→>0. So the needed lemma is true but proved nowhere; no actual counterexample exists, but as written the necessity argument is incomplete (the case of negative g-values, possibly mixed with 0 and c, is dropped), and the gap is not repaired elsewhere.
